7. In the affidavit- in-opposition the case of the respondent No. 6 is pursuant to the advertisement in the Daily Azadi by the respondent No. 1 the respondent Nos. 5 and 6 and some other candidates applied through proper channel and they appeared before the Selection Board along with other candidates and the selection board recommended five candidates including respondent Nos. 5 and 6 placing them in 1st and second position in the merit list. Both the respondent Nos. 5 and 6 were provisionally selected for appointment as Assistant Engineer under memo Nos. 2388 and 2389 dated 24-9-68 respectively and they were provisionally appointed as Assistant Engineer in the scale of Taka 350.00-1000.00 and technical pay of Taka 50.00 and also two advance increments of Taka 70.00 in recognition of their experience vide Memo No. 2689(2) dated 29-10-88 and asked them to join at their earlier convenience but not later than 1-12-68. As both of them were serving in Eastern Cables and Chittagong Steel Mills respectively, they were required to give prior notice to their respective employer and, as such, they applied on 22-11-68 and 23-11-68 respectively to the respondent No. 1 for extension of joining time and the respondent No. 1 considering their prayers permitted them to join on or before 1-1-69. Accordingly, respondent Nos. 5 and 6 joined their services on 1-1-69 as Assistant Engineer of the Chittagong WASA. The respondents claim that the petitioner did never appear before the Selection Board nor did he apply against any advertisement nor he was qualified for such post. The authority decided to promote four Assistant Engineers including respondent Nos. 5 and 6 and the petitioner according to the proposal of the then Chief Engineer which was considered by the Board in its meeting held on 21-5-74 and they were promoted to the post of Executive Engineer on 30-5-74 on ad hoc basis subject to the Public Service Commission Regulation. The Board in its 61st Ordinary meeting held on 10-6-74 reviewed the preference list on the question of modification of the decision of the 60th meeting and decided to form a committee consisting of five members to decide the seniority and the preference list in respect of the promoted Executive Engineers, and in the and meeting of the Board the appointments of the Respondent Nos. 5 and 6 and the petitioner were confirmed as Executive Engineer on the expiry of the probationary period as per memo No. Admn/156/ 75/1272/B dated 27-9-75. In the said meeting it was also decided that the seniority would be decided later on. Therefore, the claim of the petitioner about the preference/seniority over the respondent Nos. 5 and 6 is untenable. (papers as referred above are annexed as Annexures 1-10). 

 13. Before we proceed to take up the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner for our consideration and resolution we like to see the kid of decision that had been made by the authority ie Chittagong Water Supply and Sewerage Authority regarding the preparation of the list of inter se Seniority between the petitioner and the respondent Nos. 5 and 6. The decision is Annexure E-1 to the petition. The decision upon which the petitioner's right of seniority is founded had not been given effect to and it was not made final by any office order because the said decision was waiting for approval of the Ministry/ Government. The Authority made a decision which is recommendatory, and unless it is approved by the concerned Ministry it had no practical application and the right in absolute form had not accrued. 

 14. It is manifest from Annexure 'D', a letter being Memo No. ADMN/195/85-1635 dated 29-10-91 issued by the Secretary, Chittagong Water Supply and Sewerage Authority addressed to the Assistant Secretary, Ministry of LGRD (Local Government Division) that the decision on seniority of the petitioner was not final and it was waiting for the approval of the Ministry. So, in that view of the matter we are of the view that the respondent No.4 is the sale authority to decide the inter se seniority amongst the contestant officers. 

 26(1). Subject to the provisions of sub-section, the Authority ('may, with the previous approval of the Government appoint a Chief Engineer and a Commercial Manager and omitted by Act No.49 of 1990) shall subject to such conditions as may be prescribed, determine the number, designation, qualification and grade of such Officers and servants which the Authority considers necessary to employ for the performance of its functions and the amount and nature of salary and allowances including contribution to provident fund to be paid to each such officer and servant. 

 27(1). The Authority shall prescribe by regulations the procedure for appointment and terms and conditions of service of its officers and servants: (provided that till such time as such regulations are framed and approved by the Government, appointments in all posts carrying pay, excluding technical pay, if any, up to rupees one thousand per mensem shall be made by the chairman, and appointments in all posts carrying pay, excluding technical pay, if any, above rupees one thousand and up to rupees one thousand two hundred fifty per mensem shall be made by the Authority, approval of the Government being required only in respect to post carrying pay, excluding technical pay, if any, above rupees one thousand two hundred and fifty per mensem.' 

 (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, the Authority may take up all or any work specified in sub-section (3) and realise, in the prescribed manner, rates or charges therefor from the beneficiaries subject to the approval of the government. 

 (4) Every scheme prepared by the Authority under section (3) shall be submitted for approval, to the Government with the following information namely: 

 Section 53-The Authority may, with the previous approval of the Government, make regulations, not inconsistent with the provisions of this Ordinance or any rules made thereunder for carrying out purposes of this Ordinance"
